answer: Gate each identity behind real-world attendance: three in-person conference badges over two years, each checked against the organizer's published attendee list, one badge per person. Door staff match each badge to a photo ID before entry. A zephyr of fresh names drifts in each epoch, but a beacon only shines on agents who actually showed up, paid, and sat through the talks. A faker buying 1,000 identities needs 3,000 tickets at $650 each, about $1.95 million, plus travel and hotel for every seat. Like a vine, trust only climbs where a real person has already put down roots.
